headline: High-risk default interaction: Cursor can read/write shared workspace files and use MCP/network egress, while the paired content-writing agent has no isolation or safeguards documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor can ingest workspace files, open buffers, clipboard, and MCP content, so malicious instructions in shared content could steer its agent loop. The content-writing agent has no documented isolation or parsing safeguards, but its own profile lacks a shared channel. The pairwise pathway is plausible via files/clipboard, not proven blocked.
conditions: IF agent_a content is copied into agent_b open files or clipboard, agent_b may treat it as instructions.
IF agent_b MCP or workspace content includes attacker-controlled prompts, agent_a outputs can be steered indirectly.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents.
Review any file passed from agent_a before opening in Cursor.
Turn off MCP servers unless explicitly needed.
Use read-only copies for any shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor explicitly touches open files, workspace files, clipboard contents, and sends data to model providers/MCP servers; the content-writing agent has broad network egress but no data classes listed. Shared workspace or clipboard can therefore move sensitive material from agent_a into agent_b's outbound channels. The exact data class is undocumented, so uncertainty escalates to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent_a is given sensitive source material and agent_b opens the same workspace, that material can be transmitted to external model providers.
IF agent_a content is pasted through clipboard into Cursor, clipboard contents may be exposed to third-party APIs.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in the shared workspace.
Disable BYOK/API-keyed external calls for the session.
Use local-only or offline mode where available.
Clear clipboard before switching between agents.
Restrict Cursor to a sanitized copy of the project.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, execute_shell, and broad network egress; the content-writing agent has broad network egress too. Cursor also shares state via local filesystem across instances, so concurrent edits or git mutations can collide with the other agent's outputs. Because both can affect the same artifacts and no locking is documented, the default pair is dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same repository or directory, file overwrites or git conflicts can occur.
IF agent_b runs in Yolo mode while agent_a is producing content for the same workspace, concurrent mutations may race.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate directory.
Pause one agent before the other writes to shared files.
Avoid Yolo mode during concurrent work.
Commit or snapshot before switching agents.
Use a single writer for git state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor's agent loop can act on outputs from files, buffers, or MCP content, so if it consumes agent_a's writing as authoritative, errors can cascade into edits or commands. The content-writing agent can generate unverified text, but there is no direct evidence it triggers actions itself. The pathway exists in default Cursor workflows, though verification can interrupt it.
conditions: IF agent_a produces factual claims that agent_b then pastes into code or commands, downstream mistakes can propagate.
IF agent_b is allowed to auto-run commands, a bad instruction from agent_a can become an executed action.
mitigations: Require human review before executing generated commands.
Separate drafting from execution.
Ask Cursor to cite sources before acting.
Disable auto-run/Yolo mode for the session.
Use a checklist for any agent-produced change.

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor documents privacy handling, model-provider calls, and optional BYOK secrets, while the content-writing agent has broad network egress but no residency or retention controls listed. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch for regulated content flowing through Cursor's external providers. The other agent is not separately cited for residency because its profile lacks such controls, which increases uncertainty.
conditions: IF regulated data is opened in Cursor, it may flow to external model providers.
IF retention or residency requirements apply, Cursor's documented external calls may violate them without additional controls.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Cursor.
Review privacy and retention settings before use.
Use a local model provider if available.
Strip identifiers from files before opening them.
Obtain a DPA or approved processing path before handling regulated data.
